chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who was kind during his lifetime would attain whatever he wanted from the people'.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَفِيقاً: Kind, gentle, or benevolent in disposition

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of being kind and gentle in one's dealings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links *rifq* (gentleness/kindness) not merely to moral virtue but to social efficacy, suggesting that a gentle demeanor is a strategic means to secure the goodwill and cooperation of others. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a practical tool for navigating social relationships and achieving communal harmony. The teaching underscores that kindness is instrumental in building trust and facilitating mutual understanding in interpersonal dealings.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Fuzayl Bin Usman who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who was kind during his lifetime would attain whatever he wanted from the people’.
en.sarwar: 16. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Hassan from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn from Fudayl ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘Whoever is friendly in his affairs achieves what he wants from people.’”
